hint: An exponent inside a log SLIDES OUT to the front: $\log(A^n) = n \cdot \log A$.

hints.text: An exponent inside a log SLIDES OUT to the front: $\log(A^n) = n \cdot \log A$.
Slide the exponent out to get $\log_2(8^3) = 3 \cdot \log_2(8)$. Since $2^3 = 8$, the log part is $\log_2(8) = 3$. Now multiply.
Multiplying gives $3 \times 3 = 9$, so the value of $\log_2(8^3)$ is $9$.

explanation: The power rule lets the exponent move out front: $\log_2(8^3) = 3 \cdot \log_2(8)$.
The remaining log is $\log_2(8) = 3$, because three twos multiply to make $2^3 = 8$.
Multiplying the two threes gives $3 \times 3 = 9$, so the value is $9$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Just multiply it out
steps: Now ask: $2$ to what power gives $512$? Count doublings: $2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512$.
That is $9$ doublings, so the answer is $9$.
